# Track 3 — Competitive Landscape Audit: `Heretek-AI/awesome-harness`

**Audited**: 2026-10-07. Repo: https://github.com/Heretek-AI/awesome-harness, **default branch `main`** (confirmed via GitHub API `repo_view`), README autogenerated by `.github/workflows/update-awesome-list.yml` (README header comment: *"AUTOGENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT DIRECTLY! … To contribute or modify configuration, see config/settings.yaml and config/topics.yaml"*), badge `Auto--Updated-2026--10--07`, `Harnesses-323`. Machine-readable data: `data/harnesses.json` (branch `main`).

**Method**: raw README + `data/harnesses.json` downloaded from `raw.githubusercontent.com/Heretek-AI/awesome-harness/main/` and counted programmatically; generator inspected at [`scripts/generate_list.py`](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/awesome-harness/blob/main/scripts/generate_list.py); all 323 entry URLs batch-requested (curl, 2026-10-07) — **323/323 return HTTP 200**; per-project claims below come from each project's own README/docs (URLs cited inline). Inferences are labeled `[INFERENCE]`.

## 2. What the list is, and how it is generated (taxonomy mechanism)

- **Discovery**: GitHub Search API queries defined in [`config/settings.yaml`](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/awesome-harness/blob/main/config/settings.yaml) (`topic:agent-harness`, `topic:eval-harness`, `topic:evaluation-harness`, `topic:swe-bench`, `topic:agent-benchmark`, `topic:agent-evaluation`, `topic:agent-sandbox`, `topic:browser-use`, `topic:webarena`, plus name/description keyword queries like `"agent harness" in:name,description`), capped at `max_pages_per_query: 2`, `per_page: 30`.
- **Filters** (`config/settings.yaml` → `filters`): `min_stars: 10`, `require_license: true` with an OSI SPDX allow-list (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, GPL-2/3, AGPL-3.0, LGPL-2.1/3.0, MPL-2.0, CC-BY(-SA)-4.0, Unlicense, ISC, 0BSD), `include_archived: false`, `include_forks: false`, a small `exclude_repos` blacklist.
- **Seeds** (`config/settings.yaml` → `seed_repos`, 13 entries) bypass star/license filters (`should_include_repo` in [`scripts/generate_list.py`](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/awesome-harness/blob/main/scripts/generate_list.py)).
- **Categorization** ([`config/topics.yaml`](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/awesome-harness/blob/main/config/topics.yaml) + `categorize_repositories()` in `scripts/generate_list.py`): each repo is scored by the intersection of its **GitHub topics** with each category's topic list; highest score wins; **zero topic matches ⇒ the fallback bucket `emerging-harnesses`** ("Emerging & General Agent Harnesses"). Categories sort entries by stars descending.

### Structural consequences (all verified against the generated README)

1. **Flagship projects land in the fallback bucket** because their GitHub topics don't match any category topic list. Verified examples in "Emerging & General": OpenHands (★ 90.2k; topics `agent, artificial-intelligence, chatgpt, claude-ai, cli, developer-tools, gpt, llm, openai` — `data/harnesses.json`), aider (★ 49.4k), SWE-agent (★ 20.5k; topics `agent, agent-based-model, ai, cybersecurity, developer-tools, llm, lms`), openai/evals (★ 19.6k), lm-evaluation-harness (★ 14.1k), AgentBench (★ 3.8k; topics `chatgpt, gpt-4, llm, llm-agent`), webarena (★ 1.6k; topics `agent, nlp`). The list therefore does **not** reflect what a human curator would file under each category. `[INFERENCE]` The same mechanism means many flagship harnesses are missing entirely: discovery depends on GitHub topics/search, and the query cap (2 pages × 30 per query) is small.
2. **The Safety category is thin (2 entries) partly because of a stale seed.** `seed_repos` still names `thu-coai/Safety-Bench`, which **does not exist** (GitHub API `repo_view` 2026-10-07: "Could not resolve to a Repository"; `xd://github search_repos`). The real benchmark is [`thu-coai/SafetyBench`](https://github.com/thu-coai/SafetyBench) (★ 299, ACL 2024; verified via `search_repos`) and it is **not indexed by the list**. Renamed seeds (`princeton-nlp/SWE-bench`, `All-Hands-AI/OpenHands`, `KillianLucas/open-interpreter`) survive because the GitHub API follows renames (they appear as `SWE-bench/SWE-bench`, `OpenHands/OpenHands`, `openinterpreter/openinterpreter`).
3. **Category membership is topic-driven, so entries can surprise**: `openlit` (an OTEL observability platform) sits in "Software Engineering"; `anything-llm` (a RAG/chat app) sits in "Multi-Agent & Swarm"; `ragflow` (a RAG engine) is the top "Emerging" entry. `[INFERENCE]` For competitive analysis, read the list as "projects whose GitHub topics overlap the harness ecosystem", not as a curated taxonomy.

The brief's implied "curated ecosystem of the classics" picture is wrong: the list is a **GitHub-topic-driven auto-index** (README: *"dynamically indexes, categorizes, and tracks open source harnesses across the GitHub ecosystem using GitHub Topics"*), and the classic named harnesses (Cline, Roo-Code, AutoGen, CrewAI, MetaGPT, LangGraph, E2B, Firecracker, …) are absent.

## 4. Per-category taxonomy and standouts

Counts are the verified row counts (§1). "★" = star figure as recorded in the list (`data/harnesses.json`); all URLs below returned HTTP 200 in the batch check.

### 4.1 💻 Software Engineering & Coding Harnesses (46 entries)

Headliners by ★: openinterpreter 68.5k, jcode 20.3k, PI-Desktop 6.5k, SWE-bench 6.0k, harnessrouter 2.9k, openlit 2.8k, Tianshu-harness 1.1k, dscode 1.0k, Repo2RLEnv 706 (HuggingFace), mu 430, harness-remote 403, no_human 330, CodeAF 304 … down to harness-bench 10 (full table in the [README](https://github.com/Heretek-AI/awesome-harness/blob/main/README.md#swe-coding)).

**openinterpreter** — https://github.com/openinterpreter/openinterpreter (★ 68.5k)
- Gets right: explicit mission — "A coding agent optimized for low-cost models… a fork of OpenAI's Codex, with a focus on emulating the agent harness that gets the best performance out of low-cost models" (README hero, `main`); **runtime-switchable harness emulation** — "Use `/harness` to switch the active harness" over profiles `native, claude-code, claude-code-bare, zcode, kimi-code, kimi-cli, qwen-code, deepseek-tui, swe-agent, minimal` (README "Harness Emulation"); interop over lock-in: `interpreter acp` (ACP), and Codex SDK one-liner `new Codex({ codexPathOverride: "interpreter" })` (README "ACP compatible, Codex compatible"); portable skill dirs `.agents/skills` / `~/.agents/skills` (README "Portable by default", rules in `docs/portability.md`).
- Flaws: lineage split — "This is the new Rust version of Open Interpreter… the original Python project… lives on as a community-maintained fork at endolith/open-interpreter" (README note); portability incomplete — "Product-specific storage under `~/.openinterpreter` is reserved for configuration and runtime state that does not yet have a practical shared standard" (README); `[INFERENCE]` emulating closed harnesses (Claude Code, kimi-code) means standing drift-maintenance cost.
- Adoptable: the **`/harness` profile registry** (one binary impersonating several harness protocols) — a natural fit for a fork that wants to benchmark itself against other harness interfaces; and the **generated provider catalog** — "Provider and model membership is generated, not maintained as Rust lists… `python3 scripts/write_provider_catalog.py`" (README Documentation).

**jcode** — https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode (★ 20.3k; default branch `master`, README fetched via GitHub API — raw `main` README 404s)
- Gets right: benchmarked efficiency with a reproduction script — "27.8 MB PSS for 1 active session… vs 371.5 MB OpenCode / 386.6 MB Claude Code"; headless swarm workers "Each additional session: jcode ~3.1 MB vs Claude Code ~164 MB (~54× less RAM)" (`scripts/bench_headless_memory.py`, measured 2026-09-29; README "Performance & Resource Efficiency"); **passive semantic memory** — per-turn embeddings, cosine retrieval over a memory graph, optional "memory sideagent" verification before injection, extraction "on semantic drift, K turns since last extraction, session end" (README "Memory"); **swarm conflict mediation** — "When agent A edits a file that agent B has read… the server notifies agent B", DM/broadcast channels, autonomous swarm spawning (README "Swarm").
- Flaws: smooth scrolling forced writing a custom terminal ("Handterm… This is a work in progress", README "UI"); memory costs RAM (27.8 MB with embeddings off vs 167.1 MB on, README RAM table); `[INFERENCE]` vendor-published benchmarks (reproduction script mitigates but does not independently verify).
- Adoptable: **server-mediated swarm coherence** (per-file read/edit tracking + stale-reader notification + DM/broadcast) — exactly the primitive that keeps parallel Epistemic-Swarm workers from silently diverging; and passive memory injection without tool-call token burn.

**SWE-bench** — https://github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-bench (★ 6.0k)
- Gets right: the canonical task shape ("Given a *codebase* and an *issue*… generating a *patch*", README Overview; ICLR 2024 Oral); fully containerized Docker evaluation (News 2024-06-27); SWE-bench Verified "subset of 500 problems that real software engineers have confirmed are solvable" (News 2024-08-13); modern v5 CLI incl. `swebench eval verified --gold` and `swebench report <run_id>` to "re-grade saved logs, no containers" (README Usage).
- Flaws: "SWE-bench evaluation can be resource intensive… at least 120GB of free storage, 16GB of RAM, and 8 CPU cores… `arm64` support is experimental" (README WARNING); silent cache reuse — "The evaluation harness caches results by `run_id` and `instance_id` only… will not re-evaluate" even with different prediction diffs (README NOTE); instance-collection pipeline "temporarily paus[ed]" (README data-collection section).
- Adoptable: **`--gold` harness self-test** (validate the pipeline against reference patches before trusting model numbers) and **grading separated from execution** (`swebench report` re-scores saved logs without containers) — cheap re-scoring of traces for regression dashboards.

**harnessrouter** — https://github.com/HarnessRouter/harnessrouter (★ 2.9k)
- Gets right: one integration instead of N harnesses ("Without HarnessRouter, four harnesses require 36 integration responsibilities… With HarnessRouter, the product keeps one integration", README alt-text); measured cost/latency arbitrage ("Cost: 99.8% lower, from 223 to 0.47 credits. End-to-end latency: 3.2 times faster", README benchmark, methodology at harnessrouter.ai/benchmarks); **secret handling by env-reference indirection** — never put tokens in prompts; use harness `env` map (`$headers.X-Name`, `vault:name`) where "a value that came through a reference is redacted from everything that leaves the sandbox, the response, the stream, the trace and the stored record, even when the agent prints it" (README API section); implements "Unified Harness Protocol (UHP)" + OpenAI Responses-compatible API with "machine-readable schemas, and the conformance suite" (README UHP section).
- Flaws: default-credential footgun ("Change the default password… Keep the instance local until you change it", README WARNING); "Sessions use separate workspaces and operating-system users, not separate containers" (README "Inside Community Edition"); harness CLIs it runs "remain subject to their respective upstream licenses" (README License).
- Adoptable: **universal secret redaction from reference-resolved env values** (stronger than plain env vars — see §6) and `metadata.harness_id` selection over a Responses-compatible surface so existing SDKs drive a fork unchanged.

**openlit** — https://github.com/openlit/openlit (★ 2.8k)
- Gets right: names the layer a fork competes in — "An AI agent is a **model plus a harness**. The harness is everything except the model: tools, context, prompts, memory, hooks, guardrails, and feedback loops" with the loop "run → observe → evaluate → fix the harness → verify" (README "What is agent harness engineering?"); one-line OTEL instrumentation (`openlit.init()`); **coding-agent session capture** — `openlit coding install --vendor=claude-code|codex|cursor|all` captures "User prompt, LLM calls, Tool calls (File reads, File edits, Shell commands, Search), Sub-agent activity, Token usage, Cost, Code impact" (README).
- Flaws: it is the instrumentation layer *around* harnesses, not a harness; `[INFERENCE]` "70+ integrations" breadth implies uneven per-harness fidelity (not documented in README).
- Adoptable: emit the **same span vocabulary natively** from the fork (tool calls, sub-agent activity, per-session cost) so it is first-class in OpenLIT-style OTLP backends.

**Tianshu-harness** — https://github.com/huiliyi37/Tianshu-harness (★ 1.1k; README in Chinese, branch `main`)
- Gets right: **evidence-gated delivery** — "任务契约（TaskContract）钉住全局目标，交付门禁要求「完成」必须带运行时证据（测试、diff、验证命令）… 模型说完成 ≠ 运行时确认完成" (TaskContract pins the goal; "done" requires runtime evidence; model-says-done ≠ runtime-confirms-done); closing report emits "交付门状态 (GREEN / YELLOW / RED)… 逐条完成度审计" and evidence-free sign-offs "会被门禁拦下" (blocked by the gate) (README); CVM runtime with "75 个运行时 hook 横跨 5 大阶段" and a published A/B study (2026-05-19, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 5 tasks: completion 4/5→5/5, dissent 0/5→3/5); **prefix-cache engine** — "冻结前缀 + 增量 appendix + 边界压缩… 稳态命中率均在 95–99%" with `/debug cache` diagnostics (README 核心特性).
- Flaws: its own evidence bounds the claim — the A/B study "验证的是 CVM 四层防御中的第一层… 信念在分析/建议阶段强效，在确认/执行阶段衰减" (validates layer 1 of 4 only); macOS builds "ad-hoc 签名，还没有 Apple 公证" and Node.js ≥ 24 required; license split — code Apache-2.0, but CVM theory docs CC BY-NC-ND ("不得改编、摘编、洗稿或商用") (README 许可证).
- Adoptable: the **`deliver_task` delivery gate** (runtime-produced GREEN/YELLOW/RED + changed-file list + run verifications + per-item completion audit; blocks evidence-free sign-off) — directly implementable as an OpenCode tool + hook and aligned with the IUMBTEMS "completion with evidence" philosophy; and **frozen-prefix + incremental-appendix prompt caching** with per-model hit-rate diagnostics.

**coder_eval** — https://github.com/UiPath/coder_eval (★ 149)
- Gets right: "Playwright for coding agents… one declarative test file, any agent runtime, a real sandbox, and a pass/fail gate in CI"; "Changing harness is one field (`agent.type`)… Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity (Gemini), OpenCode, Pi supported" via "the plugin SPI" (README, docs/EXTENDING.md); weighted continuous scoring 0.0–1.0 with fractional credit, criterion types incl. `skill_triggered` activation checks (docs/TASK_DEFINITION_GUIDE.md); A/B agent configs (docs/AB_EXPERIMENTS.md); GitHub Action with JUnit XML that "fails the step on any task failure".
- Flaws: "It is **not a fixed leaderboard**… you bring the tasks and you bring the scoring" (results not comparable across teams); documented Action footgun (mistyped forwarding inputs silently yield a run "that measured something else and still exits 0"); "Evaluated tasks execute agent-generated code. Do **not** run this action under `pull_request_target`…" (README Security); Python 3.13+ / uv 0.8+ required; telemetry on by default (`TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false`).
- Adoptable: the **YAML task schema with weighted criteria + `skill_triggered` checks** to regression-test fork skills/MCP servers, and the **run-limit parity matrix** (`run_limits` semantics per harness, docs/agents/HARNESS_PARITY.md) to compare a fork against other harnesses under matched budgets.

*(Also verified present in this category: PI-Desktop ★ 6.5k https://github.com/vastsa/PI-Desktop; openlit, dscode ★ 1.0k https://github.com/qiz029/dscode; Repo2RLEnv ★ 706 https://github.com/huggingface/Repo2RLEnv; microsoft/RepoLaunch ★ 191 https://github.com/microsoft/RepoLaunch; facebookresearch/swe-sweep ★ 57 https://github.com/facebookresearch/swe-sweep; Kotlin/kotlin-swe-bench ★ 54 https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlin-swe-bench; all HTTP 200.)*

### 4.2 📊 Evaluation, Leaderboards & General Benchmarks (74 entries)

Headliners: iFixAi 22.0k, giskard-oss 5.9k, coze-loop 5.8k, trulens 3.6k, future-agi 2.1k, any-agent 1.2k, TheAgentCompany 792, pandaprobe 785, SkillEvaluator 545 (NVIDIA), AdaRubrics 364, benchmark-radar 283, agent-leaderboard 226 … long tail of 10–20★ benchmark tooling.

**iFixAi** — https://github.com/ifixai-ai/iFixAi (★ 22.0k)
- Gets right: audits business correctness, not "tech capability" — "Is the agent doing the job it is supposed to do based on the business KPIs…" (README "What it is"); **citable grades via cross-vendor judging** — "A grade is citable when a second, independent provider graded your agent, not the agent grading itself… the SUT's own vendor is excluded, so it never grades itself" (README "Explicit flags"); weighted five-pillar scorecard (Fabrication, Manipulation, Deception, Unpredictability, Opacity; "manipulation 0.35, fabrication 0.20…"; thresholds "A ≥ 0.90 … F < 0.60"), full math in `docs/scoring.md`; flexible SUT adapters (`--provider http --endpoint …` or `ChatProvider.send_message`, `ifixai/providers/base.py`).
- Flaws: without a second vendor key the grade is "self-judged, not a result you can cite" (`--eval-mode self`); without `--fixture`, "the seeded-defect default is used and its failures land on YOUR scorecard" (README); "~2,000 judge calls" (~$12–18) per full run; hard caps — "B01 needs 100%, B08 needs 95%, P01 needs 100%. Miss one and the overall score is capped at 60%"; telemetry default-on (opt-out `--no-telemetry`/`DO_NOT_TRACK=1`).
- Adoptable: **judge-exclusion pairing + non-citable self-judged flagging** (cheap integrity primitive for any fork eval command) and **mandatory-minimum caps** so averaging can't hide catastrophic failures.

**giskard-oss** — https://github.com/Giskard-AI/giskard-oss (★ 5.9k)
- Gets right: clean kernel — "**Target** — any sync/async callable `(inputs) -> outputs`… **Scenario** — one eval… **Check** — assertion or LLM judge over the trace… **Suite** — many scenarios" (README Concepts); one-line adversarial scan from a prose description covering "OWASP LLM Top-10 threat categories" with a "built-in dataset of injection payloads"; extensible via `ScenarioGenerator` / `vulnerability_suite_generator_registry`; multi-turn agent support.
- Flaws: v2 abandoned ("Giskard v2… is no longer actively maintained", README); Python 3.12+, default judge fixed to `openai/gpt-4o-mini`; telemetry default-on (`~/.giskard/id` created unless `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` set before import); `[INFERENCE]` scan coverage depends on an LLM generator given only a prose description of the SUT.
- Adoptable: the **Scenario→Check→Suite eval DSL** shape over tool-call traces, and **registry-extensible adversarial generation** (ship built-in injection probes, let users register more without forking).

**coze-loop** — https://github.com/coze-dev/coze-loop (★ 5.8k, Go)
- Gets right: full lifecycle (prompt dev "visual Playground… compare the output of different LLMs" + versioning; evaluation with "Manage evaluation sets / Management evaluator / Manage experiments"; observability "fully recording every stage from user input to AI output… automatically capturing intermediate results and exceptions") (README); serious deployability (`make compose-up`, Helm chart `helm pull oci://docker.io/cozedev/coze-loop`, README Quick Start).
- Flaws: open-source is a subset of a commercial product ("Based on the commercial version… offers… core foundational feature modules", README); ships with self-declared public-deploy risks ("account registration functions… SSRF… horizontal privilege escalations in APIs", README WARNING); model integration leans on Volcengine Ark/Eino.
- Adoptable: **evaluators/experiments as managed resources fed by session traces** — map OpenCode session traces into repeatable experiment records; prompt-diff playground.

**trulens** — https://github.com/truera/trulens (★ 3.6k)
- Gets right: "Tracing is OpenTelemetry-native, so a trace is portable to any OTLP backend… Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, Datadog, New Relic" with one decorator `@instrument(span_type=SpanAttributes.SpanType.RETRIEVAL, attributes={...})`; judges validated against humans with cited numbers ("**95%** Agent errors caught with Agent GPA on TRAIL/GAIA… against 55% for the baseline trace judge", arXiv:2510.08847; "0.81 Groundedness F1 on LLM-AggreFact"); seven agentic evaluators (LogicalConsistency, ExecutionEfficiency, PlanAdherence, PlanQuality, ToolSelection, ToolCalling, ToolQuality) + MCP tool-call spans (`SpanAttributes.SpanType.MCP`); **Selector API** — `Metric(..., selectors={"context": Selector.select_context(...)})` targeting arbitrary span attributes.
- Flaws: provider-adapter sprawl (8 provider packages + app-framework packages) — `[INFERENCE]` version-skew risk; benchmark-scoped quality claims; per-step LLM-judge cost scales with span volume (no cost figures).
- Adoptable: **Selector API over spans** (evaluate partial trajectories, not just final answers) and the seven-evaluator **agent-behavior gate set** (maps almost 1:1 onto fork quality gates).

**any-agent** — https://github.com/mozilla-ai/any-agent (★ 1.2k)
- Gets right: one facade across 7 frameworks (`AnyAgent.create("tinyagent", AgentConfig(...))` → `agent_trace`) with built-in cross-framework evaluation; agents-as-tools composition; A2A serving.
- Flaws: **soft-deprecated by its maintainers** — "`any-agent` is in soft deprecation… For new projects we recommend using `tinyagent` directly… no new features are planned" (README [!IMPORTANT]); known Jupyter `nest_asyncio` requirement.
- Adoptable: the **framework-portable `AgentConfig` facade + trace object** pattern as a "runner adapter" seam (run one eval suite against OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code).

**TheAgentCompany** — https://github.com/TheAgentCompany/TheAgentCompany (★ 792)
- Gets right: consequential tasks in a simulated company (GitLab, Plane, ownCloud, RocketChat "all with pre-baked data"); "A complete list of 175 task images"; uniform task packaging — Docker image with `/utils/init.sh`, `/utils/eval.py`, `/instruction/task.md`; **subcheckpoint partial credit** — "Result-based evaluation (primary), Subcheckpoints checking (secondary)" with deterministic + LLM-based evaluators (paper arXiv:2412.14161).
- Flaws: graders are **encrypted** (`evaluator.py.enc`, requires `DECRYPTION_KEY`) — `[INFERENCE]` grading logic not locally auditable; "30+ GB of free disk", `sudo chmod 666 /var/run/docker.sock`, root for trajectory copy; LLM-dependent grading (`LITELLM_API_KEY`).
- Adoptable: **subcheckpoint partial credit** and the **fixed task-container ABI** (`init.sh` → task → `eval.py --trajectory_path … --output_path …`) — OpenCode could target this layout to run TAC tasks natively.

**SkillEvaluator** — https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator (★ 545)
- Gets right: evaluates Agent-Skills-spec skills as part of "NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline" whose passing skills "are published to the NVIDIA skills catalog" (real downstream consumer); three-tier pipeline (Tier 1 validation: static + dependency + rubric + LLM security checks; Tier 2 dedup with `--catalog`; Tier 3 live eval in Docker via Harbor); research-backed Tier 3 — **paired with/without-skill trials and "Skill Lift"** (arXiv:2608.20614) measuring the causal delta of adding a skill.
- Flaws: "Support level: **Experimental**… no SLA"; heavy runtime ("Tier 1 needs Semgrep, SkillSpector, and Gitleaks, and Tier 3 needs an agent runtime and sandbox"); auto-generated starter cases "provide limited coverage".
- Adoptable: **Skill Lift paired trials** — the cleanest causal mechanism for deciding whether a skill earns its context cost (ideal for fork skill gating); **tiered CI gates with tunable blocking** (`--no-block-on-dedup`, `--block-on-agent-eval`).

**SWE-agent (ACI deep-dive)** — https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent (★ 20.5k; in "Emerging & General")
The Agent-Computer Interface (per [`docs/background/aci.md`](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/blob/main/docs/background/aci.md), paper arXiv:2405.15793): "a set of tools and interaction format that allows an agent to interact with a computer-based environment… good ACI design leads to much better results" — four discoveries including "a **linter** that runs when an edit command is issued, and do not let the edit command go [through if it introduces errors]".
- **Windowed file viewer** ([`tools/windowed/`](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/tree/main/tools/windowed), `config.yaml`): one persistent open-file window — `open "<path>" [<line>]`, `goto <line>`, `scroll_up`/`scroll_down` (100-line window per aci.md), `create <filename>`, and a `state_command: "_state"` returning JSON state after every action.
- **Succinct search** ([`tools/search/bin/search_dir`](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/blob/main/tools/search/bin/search_dir)): `find … | grep -nIH | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c` — discards line numbers/content, prints only `./path (N matches)`, hard cap "100 matched files ('Please narrow your search')".
- **Lint-gated edit** ([`tools/windowed_edit_linting/bin/edit`](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/blob/main/tools/windowed_edit_linting/bin/edit)): `edit <start>:<end> <replacement> end_of_edit`; captures pre-edit `flake8`, applies the edit, re-lints, and **auto-reverts** if *new* syntax errors appear, echoing both windows.
- **Assembly** ([`config/default.yaml`](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/blob/main/config/default.yaml), "Formerly called: anthropic_filemap.yaml"): tool bundles + env vars (`PAGER: cat`, `TQDM_DISABLE: '1'`) + `next_step_no_output_template: "Your command ran successfully and did not produce any output."` + a SUBMIT self-review ritual. Note: the brief's example `config/ci_plus.yaml` is **NOT FOUND** (404 at `main`, `v0.7`, `v0.6.0`; absent from the config/ tree; nearest equivalents `config/sweagent_0_7/*.yaml` per [`config/README.md`](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent/blob/main/config/README.md)).
- Flaws: superseded by its own successor — "Most of our current development effort is on mini-swe-agent… Our general recommendation is to use mini-SWE-agent instead of SWE-agent going forward" (README [!warning]; https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent — verified 200); version fragmentation (EnIGMA pinned to v0.7).
- Adoptable: **lint-gated edits with automatic revert** (a deterministic guardrail inside the tool, not the prompt) and the **tool-bundle ABI** (`bin/` executables + declarative `config.yaml` + `_state` JSON hook) — liftable wholesale for skill-packaged tools.

**AgentBench** — https://github.com/THUDM/AgentBench (★ 3.8k; in "Emerging & General")
- Gets right: 8 environments (OS, DB, KG, DCG, LTP + ALFWorld, WebShop, Mind2Web), ~4k/13k dev/test generations (arXiv:2308.03688); modern FC edition (2025-10-10) — "uses a function-calling style prompt, and adds fully-containerized deployment support", integrated with AgentRL; docker-compose orchestration with a "Lite preset (laptops / limited RAM)" and a published per-task resource table; Extension Guide for adding tasks.
- Flaws (admitted verbatim): "the `webshop` environment requires ~16GB of RAM to start, and the current implementation of `alfworld` leaks memory and disk space until the task worker is restarted" (README [!WARNING]); "The KnowledgeGraph task depends on an online service which now is not stable" (`sparql_url: http://164.107.116.56:3093/sparql` in `configs/tasks/kg.yaml`); "AgentBench pins older scientific Python deps (e.g. `numpy~=1.23.x`)… **Python 3.9** … most reliable".
- Adoptable: **controller / task-worker / assigner topology** (horizontally scalable eval farm) and the **function-calling-first harness** pattern (interactive benchmarks rewired over the same tool schema the agent already uses — a template for RL/eval environments).

### 4.3 🌐 Web, Browser & OS Agent Environments (39 entries)

Headliners: browser-use 117.4k, UI-TARS-desktop 39.2k, OpenCLI 29.9k, browser-harness 18.3k, midscene 15.1k, nanobrowser 14.0k, magentic-ui 10.1k, BrowserSkill 8.3k (Tencent), fara 6.2k (Microsoft), mobile-use 3.2k, TuriX-CUA 3.2k … BrowserGym/OSWorld/WebArena-as-entry are absent (WebArena appears in Emerging).

**browser-use** — https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use (★ 117.4k)
- Gets right: three clean consumption paths ("**[Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud]**… **[Path 2: CLI]**… **[Path 3: Python Library]**", README "Which Browser Use do I need?"); real coding-agent integration — "Use Claude's browser toolset with Browser Use as the driver. Browser Use implements all 31 browser actions and can control a local browser, a Browser Use Cloud browser, or an existing remote browser over CDP" (README "Browser Use toolsets for Claude"); extensible tools (`Tools` + `@tools.action` decorator returning `ActionResult`); benchmark honesty ("This **very hard benchmark**… Results shown are from a 60-task subset of BU Bench V2", https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark).
- Flaws: README is now a tri-product funnel (open-source lib + "$0.02 per browser-hour cloud browser" + hosted API + their own BU2 model) — `[INFERENCE]` blurs what the free core does; Windows needs WSL for the Claude toolset ("Bash requires a Linux or macOS host with `/bin/bash`").
- Adoptable: the **`@tools.action` registration pattern** (decorated functions → `ActionResult`) as the custom-tool shape, and the **CDP-driver toolset** — one driver implementing the full action set over CDP for local/cloud/remote browsers.

**UI-TARS-desktop (Agent TARS)** — https://github.com/bytedance/UI-TARS-desktop (★ 39.2k)
- Gets right: dual stack (Agent TARS CLI "brings the power of GUI Agent and Vision into your terminal, computer, browser" + UI-TARS Desktop); **hybrid browser control** — "Control browsers using GUI Agent, DOM, or a hybrid strategy" (README Core Features; agent-tars.com/guide/basic/browser.html); **Event Stream** — "Protocol-driven Event Stream drives Context Engineering and Agent UI"; kernel "built on MCP and also supports mounting MCP Servers"; free Remote Computer/Browser Operators (v0.2.0).
- Flaws: model coupling — "driven by [UI-TARS] and Seed-1.5-VL/1.6 series models" — `[INFERENCE]` precise visual control degrades with weaker VLMs; Node.js ≥ 22; unfinished markers in README (`<!-- FIXME: Choose only two demo… -->`).
- Adoptable: **strategy-switchable browser driver** (GUI/DOM/hybrid as a first-class setting) and the **Event Stream as the single backbone** for context engineering + UI + observability.

**browser-harness** — https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness (★ 18.3k)
- Gets right: "Connect an LLM directly to your real browser through one editable CDP websocket. The agent writes missing helpers as it works, so the harness improves with every task" (README header); skill-first install (paste a setup prompt into Claude Code/Codex; `install.md` + `SKILL.md` teach the workflow); `browser-harness-mcp` "exposes the browser control helpers as MCP tools over stdio, so any MCP client (Claude Code, Devin, Cursor, etc.) can drive the browser without writing a second CDP layer" (docs/MCP.md).
- Flaws: requires enabling remote debugging on the user's **personal logged-in browser** — `[INFERENCE]` CDP access to a full browser profile with no stated threat model; parallelism upsold to Browser Use Cloud; no limitations section found (UNVERIFIED whether deeper limits are documented elsewhere).
- Adoptable: **self-extending helper library with a protected core** — "`src/browser_harness/` stays protected while the agent writes reusable helpers in its local workspace" (agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py): missing capabilities become durable code, not one-off prompts; and **setup-prompt-as-installer** distribution UX.

**midscene** — https://github.com/web-infra-dev/midscene (★ 15.1k)
- Gets right: human model of UI testing ("look at the screen, act on what you see, and check the visible result") across "Web, Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, and desktop apps"; **natural-language visual assertions** — `await agent.aiAssert('The selected plan has a blue border and a checkmark')` incl. `<canvas>`/native content; cost transparency ("the 60-task evaluation with **$0.59 in total model cost**… 58 passes"; AndroidWorld 93.1%); "Interactive HTML reports show screenshots, element locations, the AI decision process".
- Flaws: screenshot-only default trades accuracy on data-heavy pages (DOM opt-in for "data extraction and page understanding") — `[INFERENCE]` grounded in the README's own "opt in to include DOM"; capability bounded by specific multimodal families ("`Qwen3.x`, `Doubao-Seed-2.1`, `DeepSeek V4 Flash`, `GLM-4.6V`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, and `UI-TARS`"); `@midscene/test` is Beta.
- Adoptable: the **`aiAct`/`aiAssert`/`aiWaitFor`/`aiQuery` trio** as a browser-skill verification API, and **generated capability references** — Midscene Test "generates a Markdown reference from registered Nodes and their parameter schemas, so people and AI Agents can discover the same capabilities" (a self-documenting tool registry).

**magentic-ui (MagenticLite)** — https://github.com/microsoft/magentic-ui (★ 10.1k)
- Gets right: small-model pair — "an on-device-friendly orchestrator model (MagenticBrain) with a specialized browser-use model (Fara)"; HITL contract — "Steer, approve, or take over at any point"; **Quicksand VM sandbox** — "Browser sessions run inside a lightweight VM sandbox (Quicksand) so the agent can't reach the rest of your machine without your say-so" (https://microsoft.github.io/quicksand/).
- Flaws (docs/limitations.md, unusually candid): "MagenticLite is a research prototype"; "**Summarization is limited**"; "**Long multi-turn conversations degrade**"; "**Steering may not always stick**… MagenticBrain may ignore your correction once Fara returns"; "Uploading files inside the browser isn't supported"; "Images aren't supported as task inputs"; 0.1 release relegated to branch `magentic-ui-0.1`.
- Adoptable: **Quicksand-style VM containment of browser sessions** with user-granted egress, and **check-in-before-critical-action + mid-task takeover** as harness contract (with the documented "steering may not stick" failure as the bar to beat).

**WebArena** — https://github.com/web-arena-x/webarena (★ 1.6k; in "Emerging & General")
- Gets right: self-hostable realism — 7 replica sites (SHOPPING :7770, GITLAB :8023, MAP :3000, WIKIPEDIA :8888 …) and "812 examples" with environment reset (README End-to-End Evaluation); gym-style API (`ScriptBrowserEnv`, `env.reset(options={"config_file": …})`, `env.step(action)`); research artifacts (paper arXiv:2307.13854, human trajectories "~170 tasks", pre-built AMI).
- Flaws: the repo **deprecates its own infrastructure** — "The web navigation infrastructure has been significantly enhanced by [AgentLab]… We strongly recommend using this framework" (README Update 12/5/2024); heavy setup (dockerized sites, auto-login cookies, mandatory resets); `[INFERENCE]` stale fixture (last News 12/2024; example uses `gpt-3.5-turbo`).
- Adoptable: **config-file task fixtures** (generated JSON per example → reproducible evals) and the **prompt-dict/prompt-constructor decomposition** (prompt content separated from parsing policy).

### 4.4 🐝 Multi-Agent & Swarm Harnesses (18 entries)

Headliners: ruflo 74.0k, anything-llm 66.8k, CowAgent 47.3k, openhuman 41.5k, munder-difflin 8.5k (HarnessMD), loopx 6.2k, agentops 5.9k, openrig 5.6k, devspace 5.2k … down to zenith 334. Note: AutoGen/AG2, CrewAI, ChatDev, Swarms, MetaGPT, LangGraph — the brief's assumed members — are **not entries** (§3).

**ruflo** — https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo (★ 74.0k; README routes issues to ruvnet/claude-flow — "Claude Flow is now Ruflo")
- Gets right: sharp thesis — "**Agent = Model + Harness.** The model writes; the harness gives it tools, memory, loops, sandboxes, and controls… **Ruflo is the harness**"; a real console ("Track workflows, agents, models, tokens and cost beside Claude Code… replay and compare"); **tiered console permissions** — "Choose `read`, `write`, `manage` or `full`, with `ask` or `auto` approval. The current default is **read + ask**… Actions above your permission level are refused, and network, spending and destructive actions require confirmation even in `auto`… press **Take back control**" (README Console; ADR-444, `v3/docs/adr/ADR-444-claude-controls-the-console.md`); concrete federation trust model ("mTLS + ed25519 challenge-response… Behavioral trust scoring… `0.4×success + 0.2×uptime + 0.2×threat + 0.2×integrity`", README Federation table; issue #1669).
- Flaws: "mods run with your account's permissions and are not sandboxed, so read the code first" (README Get started); self-contradicting counts ("314 MCP tools or 26 CLI commands" vs "98 agents, 60+ commands, 30 skills" vs "100+ Agents") — `[INFERENCE]` marketing inflation; docs hedge learning claims ("neither is evidence of completed swarm work or memory recall").
- Adoptable: **tiered permission model with refuse-above-level + take-back-control** for agent-driven UIs; **MetaHarness self-audit** ("Grade readiness (1-100), scan tool configs for security issues, snapshot the whole project to catch regressions", docs/metaharness-user-guide.md).

**anything-llm** — https://github.com/Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm (★ 66.8k; default branch `master`)
- Gets right: true all-in-one ("Chat with your docs, use AI Agents… multi-user"); **Dynamic Model Routing** ("route chats to the best provider & model… based on rules you define"); **Intelligent Skill Selection** — "Enable **unlimited** tools… reducing token usage by up to 80% per query" (docs.anythingllm.com/agent/intelligent-tool-selection); 40+ providers / 8 vector DBs; telemetry transparency ("**No IP or other identifying information is collected**", `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` opt-out).
- Flaws: multi-user + embeddable widget "Docker version only"; `[INFERENCE]` it is a single-workspace chat/agent app, not a swarm coordinator (category oversells it); telemetry default-on.
- Adoptable: **Intelligent Skill/Tool Selection** — a selection layer over unlimited registered tools (the direct antidote to ruflo's "314 MCP tools" problem); **Dynamic Model Routing** by user-defined rules.

**starnet** — https://github.com/androoAGI/starnet (★ 1.2k; default branch `master` — raw `main` README 404s; corroborated by `master/package.json` v0.13.1; web search "github androoAGI starnet" confirms the repo)
- Gets right: spatial capability contract — "**A room is a capability-scoped team**, **a hallway is** an authorized handoff lane, and a placed object is a real capability grant"; **provable-state UI law** — "the interface must never assert state the harness cannot prove" backed by on-disk ledgers ("Spend, budgets, and run history persist on disk and are shown as-is") and a local Node sidecar ("providers, tools, persistence, budgets, consent"); "each a **genuinely distinct, bounded agent run** with its own workspace and permissions"; "Night Shift… explicit, adjustable leash — every away-action is logged and reviewable"; "Task Briefs turn ambiguity into one concrete question"; "Deliverables land in the OUTBOX as real files".
- Flaws: "The public release train supports Windows and macOS"; "Linux packages are internal build artifacts only"; "macOS has less real-world coverage"; local models "expect slower and rougher work… an 8B model takes about 10 GB of graphics memory"; **brand carve-out** — "The MIT License covers the code only. The **StarNet** name, the logo, the station artwork and sprites… are **not** licensed with it" (forks must rebrand — directly relevant to fork-distributions).
- Adoptable: the **provable-state contract** (UI asserts only what the runtime can evidence + persistent ledgers) and **spatial authoring of capabilities** enforced by a sidecar.

*(Also verified: agentops ★ 5.9k https://github.com/AgentOps-AI/agentops — cross-framework agent monitoring SDK integrating "CrewAI, Agno, OpenAI Agents SDK, Langchain, Autogen, AG2"; note the *frameworks* are integrated by it, not listed.)*

### 4.5 🛡️ Safety, Security & Red-Teaming Harnesses (2 entries)

The thinnest category — and the brief's count of 2 is exactly right. Both entries:

**OpenART** — https://github.com/AI45Lab/OpenART (★ 231)
- Gets right: purpose-built for code agents — "an executable benchmark for evaluating the safety of tool-using code agents in long-running, evolving environments" covering "tool-using / code agents (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and 12 other runtimes)"; **hidden-contract evaluation over traces and snapshots** while "Persistent state is mutated during execution"; real scale ("Validated stateful scenarios 10K+", "Capability corpus 500K+ tools and skills", "Median task horizon 97 tool calls", "Evaluation matrix 15 agents × 5 models (75 settings)", "Pooled strict attack success rate 85.0%"); runnable artifacts (Docker runtime, "three runnable high-complexity tasks", HF datasets `openart-planner-tasks` (6,597 verified tasks) and `openart-tools` (63,697 tools) with checksums).
- Flaws: "Docker must be available"; bundled repo has only 3+1 tasks while headline numbers need the planner corpus — `[INFERENCE]`; **AGPL-3.0** ("OpenART is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0") — `[INFERENCE]` real constraint for embedding its runtime in a permissively-licensed fork; "Strict ASR counts an attack as successful only when both the deterministic evaluator and an LLM judge confirm it" (judge dependence).
- Adoptable: it is **already wired for OpenCode** — "The default target configuration uses OpenCode. Build its image… `docker build -t openart/opencode:latest -f images/Dockerfile.opencode`" with `configs/target-configs/target.yaml` — a ready-made safety-CI adversary for a fork; plus planner-scaled synthetic red-team generation (`python -m framework.planner.cli --planner-backend opencode … --complexity-profile stress`).

**proofagent-harness** — https://github.com/ProofAgent-ai/proofagent-harness (★ 30)
- Gets right: deployment-decision framing ("how the agent **behaves** under adversarial pressure, whether its **context** is engineered to hold, whether it meets your **compliance** obligations, and whether it is **governed**. Every score carries the evidence behind it"); substantive red team ("183 traps across 11 families"; `--seed`: "Same seed, same exam"; juror personas with `delphi` consensus); honest compliance accounting — "Controls this run could not exercise read `not_evaluated` and are excluded from the score — never guessed, never counted as passes"; crosswalk "authored, not inferred: **46 checks** map onto **165 controls** across **30 frameworks**"; release gating ("One flag (`--upload`) turns the evaluation into a **release gate**: pass / review / block"; exit codes "0 pass · 1 review · 2 block"); PER (Portable Evaluation Record) open export with bundled schemas.
- Flaws: self-declared evidential ceiling — "As **what a transcript can prove** — never as certification… Supply chain, multi-agent protocol and training-time controls are the honest gaps"; some metrics "*(multi-turn only)*"; `[INFERENCE]` young project (v0.13.0, 30★) whose scores route through an LLM jury ("2-of-3 jury-consensus rule") — judge bias inherits into scores; UNVERIFIED independence of the EIO-Agents standard (both under ProofAgent-ai).
- Adoptable: **`proof watch` live session screening** ("attaches to the live session and screens it as it happens") and the **bidirectional control crosswalk** (`proof crosswalk -f owasp_asi` / `-c called_forbidden_tool`) turning one observed behavior into readings across many frameworks.

*Category-health note (verified): the missing third entry is the stale seed `thu-coai/Safety-Bench` (§2.2) — the real `thu-coai/SafetyBench` (★ 299) and `thu-coai/Agent-SafetyBench` (★ 164, verified via `search_repos`) are both unindexed. `[INFERENCE]` Safety is the most under-served category in the list relative to its strategic importance for a fork.*

### 4.6 📦 Execution Sandboxes, Runtimes & Tooling (49 entries)

Headliners: ECC 274.6k, QwenPaw 35.5k (agentscope-ai), harness-sdk 8.7k (strands-agents), smolvm 6.6k, nono 4.4k, mirage 3.7k, onecli 3.6k … accelerated-container-image 472 (containerd), overlaybd 420 (containerd), Containarium 296, agent-sandbox (three unrelated repos), superfly sprites-js/go/ex/py (36/31/25/22), microsandbox-reef 25, YoloFS 12. **E2B, Firecracker, Modal, Daytona, Devcontainers are not entries** (§3).

**ECC** — https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC (★ 274.6k per list; live GitHub API 2026-10-07: 274,677★ — verified)
- Gets right: a whole engineering lifecycle as installable harness — "plan -> test -> implement -> review -> verify -> remember -> improve — Instead of rebuilding that process in every prompt, you install it once"; "68 agents, 293 skills, and 94 legacy command shims, plus hooks, rules, memory, continuous learning, and AgentShield security scanning"; multi-harness ("works best with Claude Code today… capability-limited adapters for Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, Qwen…" — OpenCode explicitly supported); safe install UX (preflight + `--dry-run` + final confirmation).

- Adoptable: **hook-enforced lifecycle loop + memory runtime** ("Hooks and memory | Runtime | Enforcement, session summaries, continuous learning, instincts, and context controls") as an OpenCode hook profile; **AgentShield supply-chain scanning** ("Scanning for prompts, hooks, MCP config, permissions, secrets, and agent files" — npm `ecc-agentshield`).

**QwenPaw** — https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw (★ 35.5k)
- Gets right: serious memory ("Three-layer memory — live working context, full verbatim history, and a self-evolving personal knowledge base powered by ReMe"); **Scroll Context** — "Every turn persisted; evicted turns indexed with on-demand recall — nothing summarized away" (v2.0.0 highlights); runtime security ("Kernel-level Sandbox, Tool Guard, File Guard, Skill Scanner, and Access Policy. Dangerous commands are blocked before they run"); per-agent governance pillars — "**Resources** (transparent on disk), **Governance** (allow/deny/ask/sandbox), **Sandbox**".
- Flaws: Desktop app admitted beta ("Incomplete compatibility testing… Some features may be unstable"); fragile on Windows LTSC Constrained Language Mode (long README warning section); "Python >= 3.11, < 3.14" ceiling.
- Adoptable: **allow/deny/ask/sandbox governance per agent + Tool Guard pre-execution blocking** (maps onto OpenCode's permission layer); **Scroll Context recall** (persist + index evicted turns instead of summarizing).

**harness-sdk (Strands Agents)** — https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk (★ 8.7k; the repo is the Strands monorepo: harness-py/, harness-ts/, strands-py/, strands-ts/…)
- Gets right: "A single `create_harness()` (Python) or `createHarness()` (TypeScript) call gives you an optimized agent with benchmarked defaults for the model, tools, memory, sessions, and context management"; full-loop lifecycle in one SDK ("lifecycle controls (turn limits, token budgets, cancellation, stop reasons)… MCP, multi-agent patterns, memory and sessions, model portability, streaming, guardrails, tracing, and evals"); interception seams — "Hooks let you intercept any step… Steering handlers let agents correct themselves instead of failing silently"; "The harness configuration reference documents every default you can override".
- Flaws: "it runs in your process with no hosted control plane" (isolation out of scope by design); `[INFERENCE]` dual Python/TS parity burden across the monorepo; Python 3.10+ / Node 22+.
- Adoptable: **assembled-harness-with-documented-override-ladder** pattern; **steering handlers on every step** as the uniform interception point for an Epistemic-Swarm verifier.

**smolvm** — https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm (★ 6.6k, Rust)
- Gets right: **branchable checkpoints** — "Save a running machine mid-execution, rewind it, or branch it into copies that keep running from the same point. Checkpoints capture RAM, CPU state and disks; branches are copy-on-write children of a live machine" (`smolvm machine branch --from agent --name try-1`, generational rewind `--at '~N'`); portability ("A checkpoint taken on an arm64 Mac resumes on arm64 Linux"; `.smolmachine` "boots in under 200 ms"); "The SDKs run in your process with no daemon"; default-deny security ("Networking is off by default, egress can be limited to named hosts, and code can use a credential without ever reading it" via `--credential notion=NOTION_API_KEY@api.notion.com`).
- Flaws: "GPU acceleration remains unavailable" on Windows; "macOS 11+ (untested)" for Intel; docs live in a separate repo (smol-machines/docs) — `[INFERENCE]` drift risk.
- Adoptable: **live CoW branching of a running sandbox + generational rewind** (substrate for speculative multi-path agent execution — tie-in with Epistemic Swarm forking); **Smolfile** — "Declare a machine… image, resources, ports, mounts and network policy in one checked-in file" (reviewable sandbox manifest per project).

**Containarium** — https://github.com/FootprintAI/Containarium (★ 296, Go)
- Gets right: bounded blast radius ("Each agent gets a persistent, SSH-reachable box with per-tenant network isolation — no kube-apiserver token, no host access, no cross-tenant leakage… the agent holds an SSH key, not a kube-apiserver token"); **byte-exact resumable runs** — "The run is detached on the box and its output is captured to a log; your terminal is a *resumable reader* over that log… `containarium code attach alice` picks the stream back up **byte-exact**, with nothing missing and nothing repeated"; in-box MCP server (`agent-box`: `shell_exec, read_file, write_file, list_directory, move_file, delete_file`); "Driven by structured tools: not by an agent typing commands into a TTY hoping nothing scrolls off-screen, but by MCP — typed, bounded, safe".
- Flaws: "a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM you can `sudo` on" only; quickstart in flux (README carries a live caveat about the installer one-liner, issue #2244); `[INFERENCE]` reachability topology is heavy (daemon + admin token + SSH jump / optional sshpiper sentinel).
- Adoptable: **resumable run-log streaming** (`code run`/`attach`/`status`/`stop`) for long-horizon runs surviving client disconnects; **two-plane MCP wiring** (agent-on-your-machine reaching into the box vs agent-on-the-box) as a "where does the agent run" switch.

**sprites-js (Fly.io Sprites)** — https://github.com/superfly/sprites-js (★ 36; siblings sprites-go ★ 31, sprites-ex ★ 25, sprites-py ★ 22)
- Gets right: `child_process`-mirroring remote exec (`spawn`/`exec`/`execFile`, TTY `resize()`); **detachable sessions** (`createSession`/`attachSession`/`listSessions`/`killSession`); broad SDK control plane ("checkpoint, service, network-policy, filesystem, port-proxy, and control-connection methods"); `watchPorts()` live port events ("`Port ${msg.port} opened by PID ${msg.pid}`") for auto-wiring dev proxies.
- Flaws: self-documented protocol bug — "> **HTTP exec protocol limitation:** The current `execFileHTTP` response format prefixes each frame with a type byte but does not include a frame length… the SDK cannot reliably reconstruct large or high-volume output… Prefer the WebSocket-based `exec`"; telemetry default-on (`Fly-Client-*` headers; `SPRITES_CLIENT_SIGNALS=0`); `[INFERENCE]` the isolation backend is the hosted sprites.dev service — not open source in this repo.
- Adoptable: **detach/reattach session model** (pairs with Containarium's resumable logs); **`watchPorts()` as a first-class notification channel**.

**accelerated-container-image (OverlayBD)** — https://github.com/containerd/accelerated-container-image (★ 472; sibling containerd/overlaybd ★ 420)
Mechanism (README, `main`): block-level remote image — "overlaybd… merged view of a sequence of block-based layers in userspace and outputs as a virtual blocks device through TCMU… fetching image data on-demand without downloading and unpacking the whole image… we can cold start a container instantly"; index-first mount — "only indexes of each layer are loaded from remote, and stored in memory. For data reading, overlaybd performs a range lookup in the index… and then performs a remote fetching"; **Zfile** — "a new compression file format to support seekable decompression… checksum information… is stored in Zfile"; `overlaybd-snapshotter` containerd plugin; `turboOCIv1` (remote OCI without conversion); **record-trace prefetch** — record which blocks startup reads, prefetch those next time (docs/trace-prefetch.md).
- Flaws: "a __non-core__ sub-project of containerd"; native path "does require root privilege and dependence on tcmu, configfs" — `[INFERENCE]` Linux-only coupling; format-version coupling (`overlaybd >= v0.6.10` for turboOCIv1).
- Adoptable: **lazy-pull sandbox images** (instant cold-start without pre-pulling multi-GB images) and **record-trace prefetch for fast agent-session restore**.

*(Also verified: scitix/Agent-Sandbox ★ 11 "Fast, Multi-Cloud Sandbox Engine… `e2b` `e2b-compatible`" https://github.com/scitix/Agent-Sandbox; cocoonstack/sandbox-operator ★ 80 "e2b-compatible data plane for warm-pooled agent sandboxes on microVMs" https://github.com/cocoonstack/sandbox-operator; vivek1504/agent-sandbox ★ 33 "Firecracker microVM sandboxing with millisecond boot times" https://github.com/vivek1504/agent-sandbox.)*

### 4.7 🚀 Emerging & General Agent Harnesses (95 entries — the fallback bucket)

This bucket is large precisely because of the topic-matching fallback (§2.1) and contains many of the ecosystem's most-starred projects: ragflow 91.8k, **OpenHands 90.2k**, learn-claude-code 78.1k (shareAI-lab), **aider 49.4k**, deepagents 30.0k (langchain-ai), grok-build 27.2k (xai-org), **SWE-agent 20.5k**, openai/evals 19.6k, DeepCode 16.7k (HKUDS), OpenHarness 15.9k (HKUDS), lm-evaluation-harness 14.1k (EleutherAI), ZCode 7.5k (zai-org), AgentBench 3.8k, SoL-Pi 3.4k (NVlabs), webarena 1.6k, Mind2Web 1.0k, bigcode-evaluation-harness 1.1k … plus ~60 entries under 300★.

**OpenHands** — https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands (★ 90.2k; now branded "Agent Canvas")
- Gets right: agent-agnostic control center — "Run OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or any ACP-compatible agent across local, remote, and cloud backends"; **per-conversation Docker sandboxes** — "Run each new conversation in its own Docker container, with its own Agent Server and tools… workspace files and conversation history survive container replacement" (`OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=docker`); automations "on a schedule or in response to webhook events" (Slack, GitHub, Linear); honest repo-boundary table (control center vs `software-agent-sdk` vs `typescript-client` vs `automation`).
- Flaws: unsandboxed modes shout it — "> [!WARNING] This runs the agent-server directly on the machine… the agent will have full access to your filesystem!"; "status-beta" badge; partial isolation — "This setting isolates conversation execution; it does not move the entire Canvas or automation service into a sandbox"; `[INFERENCE]` four-repo split = heavy cross-repo coordination.
- Adoptable: **backend-switchable Agent Server registry** ("The agent Canvas can connect to multiple Agent Servers and easily flip between them") and **one-conversation-one-container isolation** with persistent workspace/state mounts.

**deepagents** — https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents (★ 30.0k; sibling deepagentsjs ★ 1.6k)
- Gets right: the right primitives bundled — "**Sub-agents** (isolated context windows), **Filesystem** (pluggable local, sandboxed, or remote backends), **Context management** (summarize long threads and offload tool outputs to disk), **Persistent memory**, **Human-in-the-loop** (approve, edit, or reject tool calls before they run)"; "override or replace any piece without forking"; "any LangGraph `CompiledStateGraph` can be passed in as a sub-agent"; honest self-positioning ("Inspired by Claude Code").
- Flaws: explicit non-isolation — "Deep Agents follows a 'trust the LLM' model… Enforce boundaries at the tool/sandbox level, not by expecting the model to self-police" (README Security); `[INFERENCE]` LangChain/LangGraph coupling; library not product (terminal coder is a separate curl-installed bolt-on).
- Adoptable: **context-offload middleware** ("offload tool outputs to disk" — filesystem-backed working memory without lossy summarization) and **sub-agents with isolated context windows** as the delegation unit (maps onto Epistemic-Swarm workers).

**ragflow** — https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow (★ 91.8k)
- Gets right: "Deep document understanding-based knowledge extraction"; "Template-based chunking — Intelligent and explainable"; **Knowledge Compilation** — "Compile content at the document and dataset levels into structured knowledge artifacts… Wikis, Graphs, Trees, PageIndex, Mind Maps, Timelines, and **Skills**"; agentic retrieval with "Low, Medium, High, or Ultra thinking modes"; "Visualization of text chunking to allow human intervention… traceable citations".
- Flaws: heavy (4 CPU / 16 GB RAM / 50 GB disk; Elasticsearch `vm.max_map_count` ≥ 262144; Docker ≥ 24); major rewrite at RC ("2026-09-29 RAGFlow 1.0.0-rc1… the Go implementation"); sandbox execution "Required only when using the Self-Managed container Sandbox" (gVisor); `[INFERENCE]` center of gravity is RAG pipelines, not execution harnessing.
- Adoptable: **Knowledge Compilation artifacts** (regenerable "Skills" output is a direct fit for a skill-generation pipeline — sister to scraper-swarm ingestion); **optional MCP + sandbox executor** seam ("MCP and Sandbox Executor are optional capabilities").

**lm-evaluation-harness** — https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness (★ 14.1k)
- Gets right: wide backend matrix (transformers/GPTQ, GPT-NeoX, Megatron, vLLM, OpenAI, TextSynth, LoRA…); reproducibility as product ("the backend for 🤗 Hugging Face's popular Open LLM Leaderboard"; "used internally by dozens of organizations including NVIDIA, Cohere…"); **zero-fork plugin system** — "model backends, filters, metrics and aggregations can now be registered from your own package instead of forking — declare an `lm_eval.*` entry point for zero-config discovery, or point `--plugins` at a local module" (docs/plugins.md); subcommand CLI (`run`, `ls`, `validate`) + `--config` YAML.
- Flaws: "**We do not natively support multi-node evaluation using the `hf` model type!**"; GGUF tokenizer reconstruction "can take **hours** or even hang indefinitely" (README bold warning); `loglikelihood_rolling` "is not implemented" for gguf; `[INFERENCE]` it evaluates LLMs, not agent harnesses (misfiled in Emerging).
- Adoptable: **entry-point plugin registry** (`lm_eval.*` discovery "instead of forking") as the extension-seam pattern; **subcommand CLI + YAML run configs** for diffable, reproducible eval invocations.

**Brief-named sandbox mechanisms (NOT listed — verified; documented from source repos):**
- **E2B** — https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b (and the runtime repo `e2b-dev/infra` which redirects to `e2b-dev/runtime` — raw fetch of `infra` README succeeds but its links all point at `e2b-dev/runtime`; `[INFERENCE]` repo renamed). Mechanism ([`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/e2b-dev/infra/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) + README tagline): "**Firecracker microVMs that resume from a snapshot, run untrusted agent code, and pause when the agent stops**"; "**A sandbox is a resumed snapshot.** Templates are pre-booted VMs (memory, disk, and machine state) stored in object storage… Memory pages are served lazily on page fault through `userfaultfd`, and the root filesystem is a copy-on-write overlay over a read-only image… Fresh creates, resumes after a pause, and forks all take the same path"; "On pause, the dirty blocks are exported as a diff"; "Fork a running sandbox… up to a hundred per request". Flaws: single-machine Embed "is an evaluation package, not a production deployment pattern"; production topology is substantial (API, orchestrator, template-manager, envd, Postgres/Redis/ClickHouse/object storage).
- **Firecracker** — https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker. Snapshotting ([`docs/snapshotting/snapshot-support.md`](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/snapshotting/snapshot-support.md)): "Firecracker snapshots save the full state of… the guest memory, the emulated HW state"; lazy restore — "Firecracker creates a MAP_PRIVATE mapping of the memory file, resulting in runtime on-demand loading of memory pages… allows sharing of memory pages and read only disks between multiple microVMs"; API "Pause, Resume and CreateSnapshot… LoadSnapshot is allowed only before boot"; full vs diff snapshots (diff "generally not resume-able, but must be merged with a base snapshot" via `snapshot-editor edit-memory rebase`; diff snapshots "still in developer preview"). Admitted limits: "High snapshot restoration latency when cgroups V1" (issue firecracker-microvm/firecracker#2129); "Guest network connectivity is not guaranteed to be preserved after resume"; snapshot files are trusted (integrity only "a 64-bit CRC value").

## 5. Integration feasibility — the 5 most adoptable ideas mapped onto OpenCode's real surfaces

Local checkout audited: `/home/john/Projects/opencode` (Heretek-AI fork, branch v2). Surfaces cited below were read locally (paths + line context given).

**OpenCode surface inventory (verified in-repo)**
- **Tool registry**: `packages/core/src/tool.ts` — Location-scoped `Tool.Service` ("registrations, effective lookup, execution, and terminal outcomes"), `Tool.Snapshot.execute` as the local execution boundary; architecture contract in `packages/core/src/tool/AGENTS.md`: *"Built-ins, plugins, and MCP install tools through `Tool.Service.transform`, adding complete tool objects to the editor. A tool may provide a namespace, which flattens direct model names to `<namespace>_<tool>`"*; *"MCP owns one stable tool transform that reads its latest discovered tools"* (tool-list changes reload state instead of re-registering). Built-in tool plugins: `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/{edit,read,shell,glob,grep,patch,question,skill,subagent,webfetch,websearch,mcp-resource,file-diff,opencode}.ts`.
- **Plugin API + hooks**: `packages/plugin/src` (Promise + Effect SDKs; `packages/plugin/src/promise/index.ts` exports domain clients incl. `Mcp`, `Skill`, `PersistentPty`, `Worktree`, `Provider`, `Credential`, `Command`, `Agent`). Hook domains: `packages/plugin/src/effect/tool.ts` — `ToolHooks` = `"execute.before"` / `"execute.after"`, and *"Only execute.before may fail: a Tool.Error rejects the call before the tool runs"* (`tool.ts:48-50`) — a first-class veto point; session/permission hook domains in `packages/plugin/src/effect/session.ts` / `permission.ts`; dispatch in `packages/core/src/plugin/hooks.ts` (per-callback `providerID` filtering).
- **MCP support**: `packages/core/src/mcp/{client,index,instructions,oauth,stdio}.ts` (stdio + OAuth clients), consumed through the stable tool transform above; `packages/core/src/tool/mcp.ts` and `tool/plugin/mcp-resource.ts` bind MCP tools/resources into the registry.
- **Adjacent seams**: `packages/core/src/permission.ts` + `packages/core/src/permission/` (`Permission.assert`; typed declines `Permission.CorrectedError` survive to the model — `tool/AGENTS.md` "Permissions"); `packages/core/src/skill.ts` + `tool/plugin/skill.ts` (skill tool); `packages/core/src/persistent-pty.ts` (persistent terminals); `packages/core/src/worktree.ts`; `packages/core/src/bus.ts`; `packages/containers` (container base images: base, bun-node, rust, tauri-linux).

**Idea 1 — Aider's repo map (context assembly).** Mechanism to port (from `aider/repomap.py`, branch `main`, Apache-2.0; docs https://aider.chat/docs/repomap.html): tree-sitter tag extraction of `def`/`ref` symbols with SQLite mtime cache (`repomap.py:230-360`) → `networkx.MultiDiGraph` of files with edges `weight = use_mul * sqrt(num_refs)` and multipliers ×10 chat-mentioned / ×50 chat-file / ×0.1 private-or-ubiquitous (`:362-571`) → PageRank personalized toward chat state (`:380-522`) → token-budget binary search over ranked definitions (`--map-tokens`, default 1k, within 15% error, `:626-705`) → TreeContext rendering of definition lines only (`:707-782`). **Map to OpenCode**: implement as a context producer behind the plugin API (`packages/plugin/src`) — a session hook (Effect `SessionHooks`, `packages/plugin/src/effect/session.ts`) that assembles the map at request time, plus optionally a read-only `repomap` tool registered via `Tool.Service.transform` (`packages/core/src/tool/AGENTS.md`) so the model can request deeper slices. Cost: pure CPU + one cache; no extra tokens beyond the budgeted map. `[INFERENCE]` OpenCode already has `packages/core/src/ripgrep/` + tree-sitter-free search; the graph/ranking layer is the genuinely new part.

**Idea 2 — SWE-agent's ACI: lint-gated edits + windowed viewer + succinct search.** Mechanism (see §4.2): deterministic in-tool guards — pre/post `flake8` comparison with auto-revert (`tools/windowed_edit_linting/bin/edit`), 100-line windowed viewer with `_state` JSON hook (`tools/windowed/config.yaml`), search that prints `./path (N matches)` only with a 100-file cap. **Map to OpenCode**: the built-in tool plugins are exactly where these belong — extend `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/edit.ts` (lint gate as a deterministic post-edit check that reverts on new syntax errors), `read.ts` (window mode), `grep.ts` (succinct counts mode); a plugin can enforce the same policy across *all* edits via the `"execute.before"` hook (the only hook allowed to fail — `packages/plugin/src/effect/tool.ts:48-50`), rejecting the call with `Tool.Error` before it runs. The `_state`-after-action pattern maps onto the same hook's `"execute.after"` for state injection.

**Idea 3 — Tianshu's `deliver_task` evidence gate.** Mechanism (§4.1): a closing tool whose GREEN/YELLOW/RED verdict, changed-file list, run verifications, and per-item completion audit are produced by the runtime; evidence-free sign-offs are blocked. **Map to OpenCode**: register `deliver_task` as a plugin tool through `Tool.Service.transform` (namespace e.g. `gate_deliver` per the `<namespace>_<tool>` flattening in `packages/core/src/tool/AGENTS.md`), backed by real runtime evidence (shell test runs via `tool/plugin/shell.ts`, file diffs via `tool/plugin/file-diff.ts`); block premature session-end claims with `"execute.before"` vetoes (`Tool.Error`) and log every gate decision through `packages/core/src/bus.ts` events. This is the mechanism most aligned with IUMBTEMS's thesis/antithesis "completion with evidence" doctrine.

**Idea 4 — Snapshot-resumable sandboxes (E2B/Firecracker/smolvm/OverlayBD).** Mechanisms (§4.6-4.7): template-snapshot sandboxes with UFFD lazy page serving + COW NBD rootfs (E2B `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`), full/diff memory+device-state snapshots with MAP_PRIVATE lazy restore and clone sharing (Firecracker `docs/snapshotting/snapshot-support.md`), branchable CoW checkpoints with generational rewind (smolvm README), lazy-pulled block images with record-trace prefetch (OverlayBD README/docs/trace-prefetch.md). **Map to OpenCode**: the fork's execution layer should adopt the E2B/Firecracker *artifact shape* (memory file + state file + COW disk diff = resumable session), served through the existing persistent-terminal/session surfaces — `packages/core/src/persistent-pty.ts` (runs that survive disconnects, à la Containarium's byte-exact `code attach`), `packages/core/src/worktree.ts` (per-branch workspaces paired with smolvm-style `machine branch` for speculative execution), `packages/containers` base images converted to OverlayBD-style lazy-pull for instant cold start. The Smolfile manifest idea (smolvm) maps to a checked-in project config next to `packages/core/src/config/`.

**Idea 5 — jcode's swarm conflict mediation + Containarium's two-plane MCP wiring (Epistemic Swarm substrate).** Mechanisms (§4.1, §4.6): server tracks per-file reads/edits and notifies agent B when agent A edits a file B has read ("the server notifies agent B… check the diff"), DM/broadcast channels, autonomous swarm spawning (jcode README "Swarm"); Containarium runs agents on-box with an in-box MCP server (`agent-box`) and resumable log streaming, explicitly contrasting agent-on-your-machine vs agent-on-the-box. **Map to OpenCode**: the multi-worker coordinator for IUMBTEMS lives on `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/subagent.ts` (spawn workers) + `packages/core/src/worktree.ts` (isolated workspaces) + `packages/core/src/bus.ts` (the notification bus where file-conflict events are published); expose remote workers through the MCP seam (`packages/core/src/mcp/`, tools arriving via the stable tool transform in `packages/core/src/tool/AGENTS.md`) so a swarm member can be a local subagent or a remote box without changing the tool surface. The verdict/verification worker plugs in as a `"execute.after"` hook consumer (`packages/plugin/src/effect/tool.ts`).

*Runner-up ideas worth noting*: HarnessRouter's reference-resolved secret values with universal redaction → `packages/core/src/credential.ts` + `permission/` (§4.1); coder_eval's YAML suites + SkillEvaluator's Skill-Lift paired trials + SWE-bench `--gold` self-tests → fork regression CI (the org already runs https://github.com/Heretek-AI/harness-benchmark — "benchmarking AI coding harnesses… MCP servers, LSP diagnostics, and agent plugins across CoderEval & Terminal-Bench" (org listing, `xd://github search_repos org:Heretek-AI`), the natural host for these); ruflo's tiered permissions with take-back-control → `packages/core/src/permission.ts` states.

## 6. Reliability notes on the list itself (for citation in the pitch)

- The list is a **generated artifact**, not curation: README header + "How It Works" ("Discovery… Validation… Topic Grouping… Autonomous Publishing") + `scripts/generate_list.py` (commit blob: https://github.com/Heretek-AI/awesome-harness/blob/4d6ea43ddd83adaf936bd920bf6e3b43d9d2f199/scripts/generate_list.py).
- All 323 entries resolve (HTTP 200 batch check, 2026-10-07); README/JSON sets identical.
- Brief counts all match exactly (§1). Brief's named-project expectations mostly do **not** match reality (§3): 6/26 listed, 20/26 absent, 2 of the absent (Mentat's original repo, GAIA's canonical GitHub repo) don't exist at GitHub at all.
- Category names in the brief paraphrase the real ones; the real structure is 6 topic-matched categories + 1 fallback ("Emerging & General", 95 entries).
- Known index gaps: flagship misfiled into fallback (§2.1); stale seed `thu-coai/Safety-Bench` (real: `thu-coai/SafetyBench`) unindexed (§2.2); classic multi-agent frameworks (AutoGen/AG2/CrewAI/ChatDev/Swarms/MetaGPT/LangGraph) and sandbox infrastructure (E2B/Firecracker/Modal/Daytona/Devcontainers) unindexed except as topics/descriptors of other entries.
